analysis.title: Palantir: Pioneering the Sovereign AI Movement
key_insights: DB reiterates Buy on Palantir (PLTR) and raises its price target to $240 from $225. The stock closed at $178.34 on 2 Nov 2026, against a 52-week range of $107.27 to $209.05.
Total revenue growth accelerated to 96% y/y in 3Q26 from 93% in the prior quarter. U.S. Commercial grew 148% y/y, and adjusted operating margin expanded 11pts y/y to 62%.
Palantir's Rule of 40 score reached 158, the 13th consecutive increase.

DB sees AIP as the architecture connecting models with enterprise data and workflows, and the forward-deployed engineer (FDE) model as the way customers turn it into operational value. DB calls Palantir the 'diffusion layer' for enterprise AI.

Sovereign AI is adding momentum to U.S. Commercial, with AIP Evolve and model-evaluation and post-training capabilities helping customers optimize accuracy, cost and speed while keeping control of their data and workflows.

U.S. Government revenue grew 96% y/y and 18% q/q. Maven expanded beyond the combatant commands to services and combat-support agencies with more than 100K users, and TITAN moved from prototype to production after the Army's award for eight systems.

FY26 revenue guidance was raised by $378m at the midpoint to $8.530-$8.534bn, implying 91% y/y growth versus prior guidance of $8.150-$8.158bn (82% growth). Adjusted operating income guidance is $5.245-$5.249bn and adjusted FCF guidance is $4.8-$5.0bn.
FY26 U.S. Commercial revenue growth target was raised to at least 143% y/y from at least 134%.

Bears will point to decelerating remaining deal value (RDV) and U.S. Commercial total contract value (TCV) bookings growth. Management attributed this partly to shorter-duration initial Sovereign AI contracts that it expects to expand over time. DB argues faster pilot-to-production conversion shows adoption remains strong.
DB raised 2026/27 revenue estimates to $8.53bn/$13.06bn from $8.15bn/$11.38bn, and non-GAAP operating profit to $5.25bn/$7.85bn from $4.89bn/$6.84bn.

market_movers.rationale: DB reiterates Buy and raises the target to $240 from $225 after 96% revenue growth, a nine-point raise to FY26 revenue growth guidance and higher revenue and FCF estimates.

sector_views.rationale: DB sees Palantir as a differentiated enterprise AI software platform with accelerating growth at scale and a 62% adjusted operating margin.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 results (reported 3 Nov 2026 per the DB note date): total revenue growth 96% y/y versus 93% in 2Q26. U.S. Commercial revenue +148% y/y versus +149% last quarter, against a roughly 20pt tougher comparison. U.S. Government revenue +96% y/y, +18% q/q. Adjusted operating margin 62%, up 11pts y/y.

FY26 guidance raised (company guidance): revenue $8.530-$8.534bn (+91% y/y) from $8.150-$8.158bn (+82%), adjusted operating income $5.245-$5.249bn, adjusted FCF $4.8-$5.0bn. U.S. Commercial FY26 revenue growth target is at least +143% y/y, up from at least +134%.
DB estimates (forecast): 2026 revenue $8.53bn and 2027 revenue $13.06bn, up from $8.15bn and $11.38bn. Non-GAAP operating profit is $5.25bn for 2026 and $7.85bn for 2027, up from $4.89bn and $6.84bn.
Bookings softness: RDV and U.S. Commercial TCV bookings growth decelerated, which management partly linked to shorter-duration (sub-one-year) initial Sovereign AI contracts.
risk_factors: More intense competition from traditional software providers.
